absent: Numeric encodings and layouts for SMC identifier, RSI status, ripas values, GIC priority values, processor status bits and page table type masks.
Behavior of priority masking detection, priority synchronization, system register accessors, boot capability queries and virtual address size variables.
Definitions of register snapshot, static key, page table descriptors, SMC result, page change data and table walk operations structures.
Semantics of kernel table walk, leaf split helpers, contiguous split helpers, linear map indicators, update capability checks and split serialization object.
Details of TLB range limit test, range invalidate operation, global invalidate operation and repeat synchronization helper plus ordering guarantees.
Kexec image lifecycle including device tree handling, relocation use, vector installation, translation base use and zero page purpose.
Callers and preconditions for IPA state query, crash register capture, validity toggling and leaf splitting beyond what fragments show.
Full early boot table construction sequence and configuration selection among alternate macro definitions.

findings.text: Provides a synchronous query of realm IPA state over a physical interval. On success it optionally reports an upper bound address and a state value through caller supplied storage. On failure it leaves those outputs untouched. A status code is returned to the caller in all cases.

Reports that the platform provides no legacy interrupt numbers. Also advertises that deferred interrupt work is signalled by a dedicated interrupt. Header guards and compatibility selections indicate presence of backtrace and handler installation hooks.

Exposes enable and disable plus save and restore plus query operations for local interrupt masking. Every public operation dispatches to one of two back ends selected by whether priority masking is in use.

When priority masking is active the implementation adjusts the interrupt controller priority mask. Otherwise it adjusts the processor interrupt mask. Updates are ordered with barriers. Debug builds check that observed mask values match one of the two expected enabled or disabled encodings.

Disabled state is tested differently per back end. Processor mask uses an interrupt bit test. Priority mask uses inequality against the enabled encoding. Save captures the current mask then masks interrupts, with the priority variant retaining an already masked value rather than forcing a second disabled encoding. Restore writes back a saved mask with ordering and synchronization.

Provides two inline tests of a static key that yield a boolean result and transfer to a compiler generated destination on the taken path. One variant begins with a placeholder operation and the other begins with an unconditional transfer, both linked to out of line metadata.
The architecture advertises support for batched static branch updates. The size of the patchable placeholder equals one instruction word.
Each patchable site contributes a record in a dedicated section with alignment and relative references that link the patch location with the taken destination and with the associated key object.
Tag assignment and tag retrieval for address sanitizer delegate to generic tag helpers. Initialization has no effect in the examined configuration.
The identity map uses forty eight virtual address bits. Level count is derived from that width. Root level is derived as four minus level count.

Early table granularity has two configurations. One uses page shift with no skipped level. The other uses PMD shift with one skipped level. Block size is one shifted by the selected shift. Table level counts subtract skipped levels from configured totals.

Early sizing counts entries spanning a virtual interval at each level, then sums one top page plus per level contributions that include an additive allowance. Directory and device tree sizes build on that sum with extra allowances for relocatability and for segment and identity map needs.

Kernel image is described as having five segments. One configuration reserves a segment allowance equal to segment count plus two with three extra identity map pages and two extra device tree pages. The alternate configuration reserves zero in all three allowances.

Populates a register snapshot for crash handling. When a source snapshot exists it is duplicated. Otherwise general registers with stack pointer and link register are captured live, status is synthesized from exception level with stack selection and interrupt mask and condition flags, and program counter is captured at the collection site.

Defines a kexec image descriptor that carries device tree references, physical relocation addresses for kernel image and EL2 vectors, two translation base addresses, a zero page address, plus a physical offset value and a size parameter.
Source and destination and control memory limits are all unlimited. Control allocation granularity is four thousand ninety six bytes. Architecture identifier selects AARCH64.

Crash page classification always reports saveable. Suspend preparation and resume completion have no effect. Presence selections advertise support for freeing reserved ranges and for post load handling and post load cleanup.

Exposes a single page protection toggle for fence tooling that delegates to a range validity updater and always reports success. The range updater applies a transition between present valid and present invalid encodings over a page count through a common attribute changer.

Attribute changes go through a common helper that first requests a protection update then conditionally invalidates kernel translation entries. Invalidation is omitted for the specific transition from present invalid to present valid that changes no other attributes, on the basis that such entries cannot be cached.

Kernel range invalidation first normalizes bounds to page granularity and derives a page count. When the count exceeds an implementation limit it performs a full invalidation and returns. Otherwise it emits a range invalidate operation framed by ordering barriers and a synchronization step.

Full kernel invalidation follows an ordering barrier with a global invalidate operation plus a kernel synchronization helper and a final barrier. The synchronization helper orders with a barrier then performs a repeated synchronization operation.

Provides the path for changing protections over an interval. It first requests splits so the interval avoids straddling coarse leaves, then walks kernel tables without sleeping locks under lazy mode to apply set and clear masks.

Splitting of kernel leaves serializes concurrent splitters with a dedicated mutex and enables lazy mode around the critical section. The protection walk also enters and exits lazy mode around its table walk without holding that mutex.

Splitting is skipped for fence addresses and when a linear map indicator shows no special handling is needed. Otherwise the interval must be page aligned. Boot time splitting requires allocator availability and a single online CPU until capabilities are finalized. Systems lacking a specific atomic update capability take an early return once finalized.

The locked splitter optimizes the single page case by selecting the less aligned endpoint and otherwise processes both endpoints. Each address is examined from high to low levels, stopping when already aligned to a level boundary or when the entry is absent, and otherwise demoting coarse or contiguous leaves toward finer granularity before descending.

Low level presence is true when either valid or the special present invalid encoding is set. Higher level presence and contiguous properties derive through conversions to the low level entry. Leaf means present without table encoding, with configuration dependent handling for intermediate levels including a case where leaf is never reported.

Intermediate table lookup either folds to the parent when four level tables are disabled or indexes a virtual alias of the parent page at the address derived index. Virtual aliasing is defined as a physical to virtual conversion.

Four level table enablement depends on configured level count with large address support and boot capability state and actual virtual address size, choosing among always enabled and comparison against configured width and a specific large address capability.
